symptom: A member that reuses a name already on the entity's generalization chain passed `check -p` and exec, and mxbuild rejected it as CE0069 "Duplicate member name 'X'." — an attribute on a specialization named like an inherited attribute (`HR.Emp extends Other.Person (Name: …)`), a cross-module association `HR.Person_Dept from HR.Emp` beside the inherited `Other.Person_Dept`, `extends System.User (Name: …)` / `(UserRoles: …)`, `alter entity <generalization> add attribute` of a name a specialization has, a rename into such a name, and an entity's own attribute and association of one name
cause: Nothing decided 'this entity already has a member of that name' along the chain. The only CE0069 guard was dropInheritedTargets inside bulk ALTER ENTITIES, which drops a child when its parent is also a target and does not look outside the target set; create entity, alter entity add/rename attribute, create association, rename association and `set owner both` checked only the entity's own attribute list or the module's association names
file: `mdl/executor/member_name_clash.go` (memberWorld, memberNameClash — the one verdict; refuseMemberNameClash in execCreateEntity, execAlterEntity add/rename, execAlterEntities before any write, execCreateAssociation, execAlterAssociation set owner both, execRenameAssociation; validateMemberNameClashes in the check -p reference pass; scriptMemberNameClashes as MDL-MEMBER01 in project-free ValidateProgram)
insight: Measure the rule's edges before writing it, in one app with no other error — 17 shapes in a single mx check run on 11.13.0 settled it: CE0069 covers attribute/attribute, association/association, attribute/association BOTH ways, two levels up, System ancestors' attributes AND associations (System.User.Name, System.UserRoles, System.FileDocument.Size), the DOWNWARD direction (generalization gains a specialization's member), renames, and an entity's own attribute vs own association. An association is a member of its FROM entity only — of its TO entity too under owner Both (reference and reference set); an attribute on the TO end of an owner-Default association does not collide. Names differing only in case do NOT collide, so the comparison is exact, unlike validateBusinessEventInheritedMembers. Check must replay the script in order over the project's members (create, alter add/drop/rename, create/drop/rename association, rename/move entity): judging against the stored model alone refuses a drop-then-re-add and misses the ordinary one-script case, and a child created before its lazily-resolved parent is only caught by also walking DOWN from the parent when it is created. A refusal reports only clashes the statement introduces (a re-run `create or modify` of an unchanged entity is not judged), and the bulk path is judged for every target before the first write so a refusal leaves nothing behind
